name: Wyvern Spire
geological_features: Towering basalt columns reaching kilometers in height due to low gravity
Impact craters with perfectly preserved ejecta patterns
A network of lava tubes large enough to house cities
specific_features: Electromagnetic anomalies in the deepest lava tubes suggesting buried metallic structures
resources: Iron and nickel in easily accessible surface deposits
Sheltered lava tubes ideal for habitat construction
description: Wyvern Spire is an airless rocky world distinguished by its extraordinary vertical geology. Low gravity and ancient volcanic activity combined to produce basalt columns that reach heights impossible on more massive worlds, their dark spires casting razor-sharp shadows across the cratered plains. The tallest formations cluster near the equator, creating a jagged skyline visible from orbit that early cartographers likened to the ridged spine of a dragon.

Without atmosphere to diffuse light, the surface exists in a world of absolute contrast. Sunlit faces blaze white-hot while shadows plunge to cryogenic temperatures within meters. The silence is total and oppressive, broken only by the vibration of micrometeorite impacts transmitted through boot soles. At night, the spires become black cutouts against a star field of overwhelming density.

The lava tube network beneath the surface is the planet's true prize. Surveys have mapped over twelve thousand kilometers of tunnels, some wide enough to accommodate industrial installations, all shielded from radiation and temperature extremes by meters of solid rock. Deep within the network, magnetometer readings have detected anomalies consistent with large metallic objects, though no expedition has yet reached the source. The tubes branch and reconnect in patterns that some geologists argue are too regular to be entirely natural.

Mining concerns have already staked claims across the most accessible surface deposits, but the lava tubes have drawn interest from military planners and colony architects alike. The electromagnetic anomalies remain unexplored due to the sheer depth at which they occur and the risk of tunnel collapse in unmapped sections. Whatever lies buried beneath Wyvern Spire has waited a long time, and the race to reach it is intensifying.
